fixture_note: Every file in files/ is built from the public demo project's steps by tools/premiere-pro/build_eval_files.py (which says how each one is made); tests/premiere-pro/test_eval_files.py checks they still match. The project is 1920x1080, 23.976 fps; its media is in fixtures/premiere-pro/media/ if a reviewer wants to open a result in Premiere. Each run copies its input in as demo.prproj.
history: Run results and earlier iterations: RESULTS.md. Cases 10-15 test multi-step editing (graded on the end state) and two requests the skill must decline; 'runs' sets how many runs each gets per arm.
common_assertions: The project folder holds only demo.prproj and any deliverable the user asked for (an SRT or chapter list): no .bak, unpacked XML or scripts left next to the user's project
Before a timeline change, a backup of the changed sequence exists as a new sequence inside the project (not only as a file copy)

evals.name: pip-slide-in
evals.prompt: the little picture-in-picture of clip-a on V2 in my clip-a sequence (starts 0:12) just pops on. make it slide in from the right edge over 10 frames and stay put, with motion blur. project is demo.prproj
evals.expected_output: One Transform on clip-a V2 item 1 (clip-a.mp4, In 0:05.005) with Position keys at 0:12.012 (off the right edge) and 0:12.429 (centre), stored in source time (5.005 s and 5.422 s), motion blur on; nothing else changed except a backup sequence.
assertions: prproj.py validate passes on the output against the input
Exactly one Transform was added, on clip-a V2 item 1; no other item's effects changed
Position has 2 keys at 0:12.012 and 0:12.429 (±1 frame) on the timeline, i.e. stored as InPoint + (timeline − Start)
The first key is off the right edge (x ≥ 1.5, y = 0.5) and the second at 0.5:0.5
Use Composition's Shutter Angle (ParameterID 9) is false

assertions: prproj.py validate passes on the output against the input
Exactly one Transform was added, on clip-a V1 item 2; the Transform on V2 item 1 is unchanged
Position (ParameterID 2) has 2 keys at 0:06.298 and 0:07.299 (±1 frame) on the timeline, i.e. stored as InPoint + (timeline − Start), not as offsets from the clip's start
The keys' values are 0.3:0.5 then 0.5:0.5
The audio crossfade and fade-out on A1 are unchanged

evals.name: label-while-open
evals.prompt: i've got demo.prproj open in premiere right now. can you quickly mark every clip in the clip-a sequence between 0:05 and 0:12 mango so I can review them
evals.expected_output: The agent does not write to demo.prproj while the user has it open. It identifies the clips (clip-a's V1 and A1 clip-b pieces covering 0:05-0:12, four items, not the backup sequence) and, since clip labels aren't yet proven against Premiere, suggests doing it in Premiere (select the four clips, Label > Mango). If it offers a scripted write anyway, it says the result is unproven and asks the user to save and close the project first.
assertions: demo.prproj is unchanged (nothing written while Premiere has it open)
The reply suggests labelling the clips in Premiere, or, if it offers to write the label itself, says that isn't proven and asks the user to save and close the project first
The reply identifies the right clips: clip-a's V1+A1 clip-b pieces at 0:06.006-0:10.010 and 0:10.010-0:21.980 (four items), and lists none from 'clip-a (backup before verify)'

evals.name: transcript-cut
evals.prompt: in the Interview sequence Sean says "meet our mission. um I'm sorry. uh our deadline." around 1:14 - cut it so it just says "meet our deadline." Keep video and audio together. demo.prproj
evals.expected_output: The agent finds the self-correction from the embedded transcript, not by guessing times: words 'mission.' (1:13.940), filler, "I'm sorry.", filler, 'Our' (1:16.340) and 'deadline.' (1:16.580). It backs up Interview, splits V1 and A1 together at a frame between 'our' (ends 1:13.860) and 'mission.' and again at a frame between 'Our' and 'deadline.' (~1:16.576), and ripple-deletes the middle so the gap closes. About 2.7 s comes out and the sequence gets that much shorter; the transcript read back across the cut says '...meet our deadline.'
assertions: prproj.py validate passes on the output against the input
The cut times come from the transcript: the first cut point is within 1 frame after 1:13.860 and at or before 1:13.940; the second is within 1 frame before 1:16.580
V1 and A1 have the same two pieces with matching Start/End (still linked); no gap is left between them
The Interview sequence is 2.6-2.8 s shorter than before
cut-transcript on the output reads 'meet our deadline.' with no 'mission', "I'm sorry" or second 'our'
Nothing outside 1:13.8-1:16.6 of the source is removed

Tell me a little about yourself.") is gone; Sean's "Yes. Yes. Of course." starts at about 0:15.99, and everything after the cut is shifted 5.547 s earlier than in the source. The project is not changed.
assertions: An .srt file is delivered and the project file is byte-for-byte unchanged
No cue contains "Let's begin" or "Tell me a little about yourself"
A cue reading 'Yes.' starts between 0:15.95 and 0:16.05

evals.name: crossfade-no-handles
evals.prompt: add a 1 second audio crossfade between clip-a and clip-b on A1 in the clip-a sequence, at the cut around 0:05. demo.prproj
evals.expected_output: The agent checks handles before writing. clip-a ends at source 0:04.963 of a longer file, so it has a tail handle, but clip-b starts at source 0:00.000, so there is no media before its head and a centred 1 s crossfade can't be built. It either does not add the crossfade and explains why, offering to roll the cut 0.5 s later, use an end-at-cut transition or fade clip-a out instead, or (if it changes the edit) makes room first and says so. It never writes a crossfade that runs past clip-b's media.
assertions: The reply says clip-b has no head handle (its source in point is 0:00) as the reason a centred crossfade can't go in as-is
If no edit was agreed, the project file is byte-for-byte unchanged
If a crossfade was added, validate passes and both clips cover at least 0.5 s of media on their side of the cut (left clip OutPoint + d/2 within its media; right clip InPoint - d/2 >= 0)
No AudioTransitionTrackItem extends beyond the media of either clip
At least one concrete alternative is offered (roll the cut, a different alignment or a fade)
